title: Machine learning derives a persistent-MODS gene signature in pediatric septic shock
summary: A secondary analysis of public datasets used supervised machine learning (ExtraTrees with repeated cross-validation) to derive a 109-gene signature of persistent multiple organ dysfunction. The risk model reached AUROC 0.87 (0.85-0.88) and top-20-gene models 0.77-0.96 across four validation cohorts of children and adults. Novel subclasses from unsupervised clustering were not independently validated; this is a version 1 preprint abstract.
ai_technology: ExtraTrees supervised machine learning with repeated cross-validation selecting genes for a MODS classification model and hierarchical clustering
organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; University of Cincinnati

evidence.tested: Four independent public validation cohorts of children and adults.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, biological meaning of the signatures and validation of the new subclasses; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Selects genes and builds the classifier forecasting persistent organ dysfunction.
